content.text:
I've finished and submitted **index 14 (In 0.53 / Sb 0.47)**. It had the highest efficiency I measured, at 0.0361%. I used all 3 efficiency measurements and 2 of the 5 X-ray (XRD) scans.

| Index | In / Sb | Efficiency (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.87 / 0.13 | 0.0169 |
| 14 | 0.53 / 0.47 | **0.0361** |
| 18 | 0.40 / 0.60 | 0.0357 |

- **Trend:** efficiency roughly doubles from the In-rich end to the middle, then flattens. Index 18 is effectively the same as index 14, so the best spot is somewhere in the In 0.40–0.53 range.
- **X-ray scans:** index 14 and index 22 (In 0.27) are both mainly the same 1:1 In–Sb oxide (InSbO4). Index 22 also shows two extra peaks, which point to a second phase. With the efficiency already levelling off, I didn't spend the last measurement further toward the Sb-rich end.
- **Not measured:** the Sb-rich end past index 18 (indices 19–27) and the In-rich side between indices 1 and 13. A better composition could exist there, but the trend doesn't suggest one.
